prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
*(Adjusts microphone, clears throat, stares resolutely at the panel)*

Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee. Let me begin by stating for the record that I love this country, and I love a mid-summer neighborhood potluck. I believe in the sacred, cellophane-wrapped institutions that make our cul-de-sacs great. 

But I will not sit here and be the victim of a culinary witch hunt.

You have called me before this committee to answer to whispers, rumors, and neighborhood gossip. You ask, "Are you now, or have you ever been, a purchaser of grocery store deli sides?" 

The accusation is that on the afternoon of July 4th, at the Petersons' residence, I knowingly and maliciously transferred a two-pound tub of Publix macaroni salad into a vintage Cornflower Blue CorningWare dish, thereby committing an act of suburban subversion. 

Mr. Chairman, this committee has been fed lies. 

I will admit only to this: I was pressed for time. The humidity was ninety percent. I was operating under the stress of ensuring the inflatable pool was properly inflated. Did I seek out a base element from the local supermarket? Perhaps. But I reject the committee’s assertion that it was quote-unquote "store-bought." 

I ask you, gentlemen: Is a dish "store-bought" if it has been doctored? 

I chopped celery, Mr. Chairman! I added fresh dill! I sprinkled smoked paprika across the top in a decorative, zig-zag pattern that screamed "sweated over a hot stove!" I wiped the mayonnaise smudges off the rim of my Pyrex with a damp paper towel so that it looked immaculate. Does the addition of a heavy paprika garnish not constitute homemade preparation under the laws of this land? 

*(Pounds fist lightly on the table)*

If taking a foundational deli salad, customizing its flavor profile, and serving it at room temperature makes me un-American, then I no longer know what this country stands for. 

I know what the committee really wants. You want me to name names. You want me to tell you who brought the Costco croissants and put them in a wicker basket with a gingham cloth. You want me to give up the individual who took a frozen Marie Callender's pie, crumbled extra graham crackers on it, and called it their grandmother’s recipe. 

Well, I will not do it. I refuse to turn on my neighbors. I will not point my finger at Linda from across the street just to save my own skin, even if everyone *knows* her pulled pork is just defrosted Lloyd's from a plastic tub!

*(Takes a sip of water, straightens tie)*

I stand by my macaroni salad. It was the first side dish to be completely eaten, beating out Mrs. Peterson’s dry, raisin-infested coleslaw. I will answer no further questions on this matter, and I assert my Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination. 

But for the record... I need my CorningWare back.
